mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP (GDPC1) signals stronger economic demand, which drives corporate earnings and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 forward returns are negative during periods of GDP growth, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 3% annualized rate signals inflationary pressures that may lead to monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 forward returns remain positive despite sustained CPI increases above 3%, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment (UNRATE) combined with a decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals labor market weakness, which may lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 forward returns are positive despite rising unemployment and falling payroll employment, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals stronger supply-side activity, which may lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 forward returns are negative during periods of industrial production growth, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 1% signals monetary easing, which may lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 forward returns do not increase despite a decline in FEDFUNDS below 1%, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals stronger demand in the housing market, which may lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 forward returns are negative despite an increase in housing starts, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in retail sales (RSAFS) combined with an increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals strong demand and supply-side activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 forward returns are negative despite increases in both retail sales and industrial production, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% signals a tight labor market, which may lead to wage inflation and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 forward returns remain positive despite sustained low unemployment, this hypothesis is rejected.
